integrity: The finite theorem is proved only from two path involutions, with no appeal to an independence approximation. The checker includes dependent nonexchangeable orbit-mixture laws to ensure that the proof is not silently using exchangeability. The asymptotic correlation is separated from the exact theorem and uses a standard invariance-principle argument with moment uniform integrability.
scientific_limitations: The exact identity needs both reversal invariance and global sign symmetry of the finite increment vector.

The iid half-variance special case is already implicit in classical joint maximum/endpoint fluctuation theory; the claimed new scope is the weak-symmetry dependent setting and the odd-transform family.
The correlation limit additionally assumes an iid symmetric increment law with a finite moment of order strictly larger than two.
title: Reversal and sign symmetry force a half-variance maximum–endpoint law
